The theorem that every rearrangement of an absolutely convergent real series has the same sum appears exactly in the cited notes; the proof is the standard finite-tail argument.

Donaldson and Hunter support the classical real Riemann rearrangement theorem. Fisher's Theorem 4.9.4 explicitly gives the stronger prescribed extended-real liminf/limsup form; the item expands it into a bespoke recursive construction with local conventions.
The exact real-series equivalence between absolute convergence and invariance under every rearrangement is stated in Hunter §4.8; the proof combines the two directions locally.

The anti-diagonal convolution definition is standard, but the item adopts zero-based local notation and explanatory scope prose.

Gardner's Theorem 7-17 gives Mertens' one-absolutely-convergent-factor hypothesis and the product-of-sums conclusion. The item packages the theorem with a local finite triangular identity and expanded proof. This live source supersedes the inaccessible JHU real-analysis PDF.

The cited Princeton text gives the exact absolute double-series theorem and equality of both iterated sums; the proof is adapted to the library's enumeration.
